arxiv-1803-08019.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Andrei Bulatov \rsuper a, Peter Mayr \rsuper b, Ágnes Szendrei \rsuper b. The subalgebra membership problem is the problem of deciding if a given element belongs to an algebra given by a set of generators. This is one of the best established computational problems in algebra. We consider a variant of this problem, which is motivated by recent progress in the Constraint Satisfaction Problem, and is often referred to as the Subpower Membership Problem (SMP).

arxiv-2201-04326.title: Time-resolved spectroscopy on the heartbeat state of GRS 1915+105 using AstroSat Time-resolved spectroscopy on the heartbeat state of GRS 1915+105 using AstroSat – References
arxiv-2201-04326.creator: Divya Rawat, Ranjeev Misra, Pankaj Jain, J. S. Yadav
arxiv-2201-04326.description: Abstract AstroSat spectra of the black hole system GRS 1915+105 during the heartbeat state (with a varying oscillation period from 150 to 100 secs) were analysed using a truncated relativistic disc model along with a Comptonization component. Spectra were fitted for segments of length ∼ 24 \sim 24 secs.

arxiv-2305-07281.title: The Spatially Resolved Properties of the GW170817 Host Galaxy
arxiv-2305-07281.creator: Yubin Li, Jirong Mao, Jianbo Qin, Xianzhong Zheng, Fengshan Liu, Yinghe Zhao, Xiaohong Zhao
arxiv-2305-07281.description: Abstract GW170817 is the unique gravitational-wave (GW) event that is associated to the electromagnetic (EM) counterpart GRB 170817A. NGC 4993 is identified as the host galaxy of GW170817/GRB 170817A. In this paper, we particularly focus on the spatially resolved properties of NGC 4993.

arxiv-2310-17570.title: DiffS2UT: A Semantic Preserving Diffusion Model for Textless Direct Speech-to-Speech Translation
arxiv-2310-17570.creator: Yongxin Zhu, Zhujin Gao, Xinyuan Zhou, Zhongyi Ye, Linli Xu
arxiv-2310-17570.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yongxin Zhu, Zhujin Gao, Xinyuan Zhou, Zhongyi Ye, Linli Xu. While Diffusion Generative Models have achieved great success on image generation tasks, how to efficiently and effectively incorporate them into speech generation especially translation tasks remains a non-trivial problem. Specifically, due to the low information density of speech data, the transformed discrete speech unit sequence is much longer than the corresponding text transcription, posing significant challenges to existing auto-regressive models.

arxiv-2311-12635.creator: Djamel eddine Kebiche
arxiv-2311-12635.description: Abstract . We present in this paper a new way to define weighted Sobolev spaces when the weight functions are arbitrary small. This new approach can replace the old one consisting in modifying the domain by removing the set of points where at least one of the weight functions is very small.

arxiv-2402-19224.title: Minimal SU(5) theory on the edge: the importance of being effective
arxiv-2402-19224.creator: Goran Senjanović, Michael Zantedeschi
arxiv-2402-19224.description: Abstract It is well known that the minimal renormalizable S ​ U ​ ( 5 ) SU(5) grand unified theory is ruled out: it predicts same masses of down quarks and charged leptons, the gauge couplings do not unify and neutrinos are massless. We show here that all this can be cured simultaneously by the addition of higher-dimensional effective operators.

arxiv-2409-03358.title: MouseSIS: A Frames-and-Events Dataset for Space-Time Instance Segmentation of Mice
arxiv-2409-03358.creator: Friedhelm Hamann, Hanxiong Li, Paul Mieske, Lars Lewejohann, Guillermo Gallego
arxiv-2409-03358.description: Abstract Enabled by large annotated datasets, tracking and segmentation of objects in videos has made remarkable progress in recent years. Despite these advancements, algorithms still struggle under degraded conditions and during fast movements. Event cameras are novel sensors with high temporal resolution and high dynamic range that offer promising advantages to address these challenges.

arxiv-2505-14799.title: Existence theory for elliptic equations of general exponential nonlinearity on finite graphs
arxiv-2505-14799.creator: Bobo Hua, Linlin Sun, Jiaxuan Wang
arxiv-2505-14799.description: Abstract . We study semilinear elliptic equations on finite graphs with fully general exponential nonlinearities, thereby extending classical equations such as the Kazdan-Warner and Chern-Simons equations. A key contribution of this work is the development of new techniques for deriving a priori estimates in this generalized setting, which reduce the original finite graph to a graph with only two vertices.

arxiv-2505-24558.title: Optimal Weighted Convolution for Classification and Denosing
arxiv-2505-24558.description: Abstract We introduce a novel weighted convolution operator that enhances traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) by integrating a spatial density function into the convolution operator. This extension enables the network to differentially weight neighbouring pixels based on their relative position to the reference pixel, improving spatial characterisation and feature extraction.

arxiv-2507-10708.title: Grammatical Structure and Grammatical Variations in Non-Metric Iranian Classical Music
arxiv-2507-10708.creator: Maziar Kanani School of Computer Science University of Galway Galway, Ireland m.kanani1@universityofgalway.ie Seán O’Leary School of Computer Science TU Dublin Dublin, Ireland sean.oleary@tudublin.ie James McDermott School of Computer Science University of Galway Galway, Ireland james.mcdermott@univ
arxiv-2507-10708.description: Abstract In this study we introduce a symbolic dataset composed of non-metric Iranian classical music, and algorithms for structural parsing of this music, and generation of variations. The corpus comprises MIDI files and data sheets of Dastgah Shour from Radif Mirza Abdollah, the foundational repertoire of Iranian classical music.

arxiv-2509-11419.title: Knowledge Distillation for Sensing-Assisted Long-Term Beam Tracking in mmWave Communications
arxiv-2509-11419.creator: Mengyuan Ma, Nhan Thanh Nguyen, Nir Shlezinger, Yonina C. Eldar, A. Lee Swindlehurst, Markku Juntti
arxiv-2509-11419.description: Abstract Infrastructure-mounted sensors can capture rich environmental information to enhance communications and facilitate beamforming in millimeter-wave systems. This work presents an efficient sensing-assisted long-term beam tracking framework that selects optimal beams from a codebook for current and multiple future time slots. We first design a large attention-enhanced neural network (NN) to fully exploit past visual observations for beam tracking.

arxiv-2602-03386.title: An Approximate Ascent Approach To Prove Convergence of PPO
arxiv-2602-03386.creator: Leif Döring, Daniel Schmidt, Moritz Melcher, Sebastian Kassing, Benedikt Wille, Tilman Aach, Simon Weissmann
arxiv-2602-03386.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Leif Döring, Daniel Schmidt, Moritz Melcher, Sebastian Kassing, Benedikt Wille, Tilman Aach, Simon Weissmann. Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) is among the most widely used deep reinforcement learning algorithms, yet its theoretical foundations remain incomplete. Most importantly, convergence and understanding of fundamental PPO advantages remain widely open. Under standard theory assumptions we show how PPO’s policy update scheme (performing multiple epochs of minibatch updates on multi-use rollouts with a surrogate gradient) can be interpreted as approximated policy gradient ascent.

pmc-10605395.title: Research on a New Intelligent and Rapid Screening Method for Depression Risk in Young People Based on Eye Tracking Technology
pmc-10605395.creator: Zhanbo Tao, Ningxia Sun, Zhen Yuan, Zeyuan Chen, Jiakang Liu, Chen Wang, Shuwu Li, Xiaowen Ma, Bin Ji, Kai Li
pmc-10605395.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Depression is a prevalent mental disorder, with young people being particularly vulnerable to it. Therefore, we propose a new intelligent and rapid screening method for depression risk in young people based on eye tracking technology. We hypothesized that the “emotional perception of eye movement” could characterize defects in emotional perception, recognition, processing, and regulation in young people at high risk for depression.

pmc-10797232.title: Benign and malignant prostate neoplasms show different spatial organization of collagen
pmc-10797232.creator: Taras Zadvornyi, Nataliia Lukianova, Oleksandr Mushii, Anna Pavlova, Olena Voronina, Vasyl Chekhun
pmc-10797232.description: AimTo compare the indicators of the spatial organization of collagen and its regulating factors between benign and malignant prostate neoplasms.MethodsThe study involved tumor tissue samples from 40 patients with stage II-III prostate cancer (PCa) and 20 patients with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). The localization of collagen was determined with a Masson trichrome stain.

pmc-11563720.title: Which infectious diseases are currently posing problems in the Republic of Korea? One out of every two tuberculosis patients is over 65 years old
pmc-11563720.creator: Jong-Koo Lee
pmc-11563720.description: Our country has made significant strides in tuberculosis management compared to other countries globally. However, as of 2023, there are still 20,000 new cases and 1,000 deaths annually. The national tuberculosis management system, initiated in 1962, led to a dramatic decrease in the number of patients through nationwide screenings, early detection and treatment, and ongoing management via health centers.

pmc-11612527.title: Age Variation Among US Adults’ Social Media Experiences and Beliefs About Who Is Responsible for Reducing Health-Related Falsehoods: Secondary Analysis of a National Survey
pmc-11612527.creator: Prathyusha Galinkala, Elise Atkinson, Celeste Campos-Castillo, Yun Jiang
pmc-11612527.description: BackgroundWe live in a digital age where social media has become an essential part of people’s lives. It is also one of the leading platforms responsible for spreading health-related falsehoods. This study explores who adults of different age groups perceive as responsible for reducing health-related falsehoods on social media.

pmc-12594952.title: Constraints of middle-late Permian granites in Eastern Inner Mongolia on the final subduction of the Paleo Asian Ocean
pmc-12594952.creator: Changji Zhao, Yunliang Yu, Yingchun Liu, Hongchen Cai, Jinxin He, Xiangwei Gao
pmc-12594952.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The Xilinhot region, located in the eastern segment of the Xingmeng orogenic belt, represents a key area for investigating the evolutionary history of the Paleo-Asian Ocean due to its close association with Late Paleozoic subduction–accretion processes. However, significant controversy remains regarding the final timing of the Paleo-Asian Ocean’s evolution and closure, resulting in divergent interpretations of the Permian tectonic setting in this region, including models of subduction, post-collisional extension, and intraplate stretching.

pmc-13112582.creator: Tabitha G. Moe
pmc-13112582.description: Corresponding Author Congenital heart disease (CHD) is no longer solely a pediatric condition. pmc-13126637.title: A Reinforcement Learning-Guided Genetic Algorithm Integrating Medicinal Chemistry-Inspired Molecular Transformations
pmc-13126637.creator: Domenico Alberga, Vittoria Nanna, Maria Giovanna Eva Papadopoulos, Adolfo Ancona, Maria Cristina Lomuscio, Giuseppe Felice Mangiatordi
pmc-13126637.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Achieving optimal target activity while maintaining synthetic accessibility and drug-likeness represents a major challenge in computational drug discovery. Existing de novo generative models often yield chemically invalid or synthetically intractable structures and struggle to optimize multiple objectives simultaneously. Here, we introduce ALCHIMIA, an interpretable hybrid framework combining reinforcement learning (RL) and a genetic algorithm (GA), built based on a vocabulary of 33 medicinal chemistry-inspired molecular transformations.
